ledger.why: the Farming or Building effects on the ending page

items.text: The villagers lay a stable, accessible path, taking care not to damage the plants. The elder thanks them.
The first design would uproot an important plant. The elder explains why it matters; the builders revise it.
A child decorates the path with pebbles. The result is charming but uneven. The builders adjust it for safety.
The elder insists (elder.he/she) can manage alone. The younger villager respects the answer and offers help if wanted.
The elder recalls a friend who planted the first seeds.
The elder admits the garden was originally a failed experiment. "It was ugly. We loved it anyway."
The elder laughs about an argument over where to plant a single flower. The argument lasted three days.
The elder says some memories are private. The younger villager accepts that without pressing.
The younger villager visits again the next morning. This time, they work quietly side by side.
The elder gives the child a seed and explains how to care for it.
The garden remains small. Its meaning does not.
The elder sits in the shade, listening to the leaves.
A flower blooms in an unexpected place. The elder smiles, and for a moment looks very young.

question.name: The small garden
question.text:
An older villager, (Elder), has been tending a small garden near the Tree of Life. The garden is not particularly productive, but (elder.he/she) visits it every morning.
A younger villager, (Young), asks why.
"Because I planted it with someone I loved," says the elder.
(Young) notices that the path is difficult to walk, especially for villagers who move more slowly or need assistance.

choices.label: IMPROVE THE PATH WITH THE ELDER'S PERMISSION.
ASK THE ELDER TO TELL THE GARDEN'S STORY.
